prompt: Which statement correctly gives the definition of a random error according to the Cambridge 9702 syllabus?
options: An error that causes measurements to be consistently offset from the true value in the same direction.
The smallest change in a physical quantity that a measuring instrument can detect.
An unpredictable variation in repeated measurements that causes readings to scatter about the true value.
A constant non-zero reading shown by an instrument when the true quantity being measured is zero.

answer.explanation: A random error is defined as an unpredictable variation in repeated measurements that causes readings to scatter about the true value.

distractor_explanations: Correct. Random errors cause unpredictable variation resulting in scatter around the true value.
hints: Look for the key words describing unpredictable variation and scatter.
Distinguish random variation from constant directional shifts.
solution: A random error is an unpredictable variation in repeated measurements that causes readings to scatter about the true value.
teacher_walkthrough: Recall the controlled definition from the syllabus.
Random errors cause unpredictable fluctuations (scatter) in readings.

provenance.independence_statement: Authored to test verbatim recall of the Cambridge random error definition.
